fields.meta_title: Employee Feedback Form Builder for Staff Input | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an employee feedback form that sends each answer to the person who can act on it and shows staff what happened next.
fields.h1: Build an Employee Feedback Form Someone Acts On
fields.hero_description: Describe what staff should be able to raise and who handles each topic. Emergent builds the employee feedback form, routes every answer to its owner and keeps a record of the reply.
fields.features_heading: Six Parts That Give Each Answer an Owner
fields.features_subheading: A template collects answers and stops there. These six parts give every answer an owner and send the employee a reply.
fields.feature_1:
Answers routed by topic to one owner

Send equipment problems to the facilities lead and pay questions to payroll. Each topic has one named owner, and nothing sits in a shared HR inbox while people decide whose it is.
fields.feature_2:
A status the employee can follow

Give every submission a status of received, assigned or fixed, with the owner's reply attached. The person who raised it sees each change without chasing anyone for an update.
fields.feature_3:
A QR code for staff without a desk

Print a QR code for the break room so staff without a company email can answer on their own phones. Ask for an employee number instead of a login and keep the form to a few taps.
fields.feature_4:
Check-ins sent on a schedule

Send the form on a new hire's 30th day or the evening before each one-on-one. A reminder goes to anyone who has not answered after two days, and it stops as soon as they do.
fields.feature_5:
Open items sorted by team and age

Filter every answer by department or location, then sort open items by how long they have waited. HR sees which team raised the most this month and which replies are overdue.
fields.feature_6:
The codebase in your GitHub repository

Export the full code to your GitHub repository when feedback records belong beside your HR data. Your developers can host the app on your own servers and keep extending it.
fields.why_title: Why Run Employee Feedback on Emergent?
fields.why_description: A paper form in a suggestion box gets read when someone remembers to open it. Staff stop writing once nothing they raise gets an answer.

fields.tab_content_1:
No HR detour for a sticking dock door

Most pickers at Harlow Provisions have no company email. A QR code in the break room opens the form on their own phones, starting with a topic. A report that the bay 6 dock door sticks went straight to Marcus Bell, the facilities lead. The picker saw the status change to fixed once the door was repaired.
fields.tab_content_2:
IT hears when a laptop shows up late

Every new hire at Quillon Software gets a short check-in on their 30th day. It asks whether the laptop, accounts, desk and onboarding buddy were ready when they started. Dana Whitlock said her laptop arrived on day 3. Sam Ortega, the IT lead, got a message, and HR tracks the answers by start month.
fields.tab_content_3:
A blocker carried into every Tuesday until fixed

Before each Tuesday one-on-one, engineers at Fernhill Labs list what shipped and what is stuck. Their manager, Nora Lindqvist, reads the answers the evening before. One blocker, no access to the staging server, has sat on her agenda for 3 weeks. It comes back every Tuesday until she marks it resolved.
fields.tab_content_4:
Imaging wrote 14 of 46 comments, all about weekends

Westmere Clinics opened its draft on-call schedule to staff comments until Friday. The form asks for a department and one comment per section. By the deadline, 46 comments had come in from 5 departments. Ruth Calloway, the operations director, read the 14 from imaging first: every one concerned weekend coverage.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Employee Feedback Form
fields.howto_description: Settle who answers each kind of comment before you write a single question.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Print the reply promise on the form
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the topics staff are likely to raise, such as equipment, scheduling, pay and policy, and put one person's name beside each. A topic with no owner turns into a pile of unread answers. Merge any topics that would land with the same person.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose before launch whether answers carry a name. Named answers let the owner follow up with questions. Anonymous ones bring out problems people will not sign. If you need both, run two forms and state on each one exactly what is stored.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Someone filling this in on a break should finish in two minutes. Lead with the topic, then ask one open question about what happened and one about what would fix it. Add a rating scale only when you plan to track that number over time.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell staff who will reply and how fast, for example within five working days. Then keep that promise every time. A form that never answers teaches people to stop writing, however good its questions are.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Describe the topics, the owners, the reminders and where a reply should appear. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it and a dashboard for HR. Change a question or add a topic later by asking for it in one sentence.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Put the link where people work
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pin the link in the team Slack channel and print a QR code for staff who work without a desk. Send scheduled check-ins, like the 30-day onboarding form, from the same app so every answer lands in one database.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test the loop from a phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a test answer from a phone under each topic. Check that the right owner gets the message and that the employee sees the reply once the status changes. Delete the test answers before you share the link with staff.

plan.angle: The live results lead with evaluation templates from LimeSurvey, Jotform and forms.app, then a Pinterest pin of Word review forms, a Template.net onboarding survey, an Engagedly tools listicle and a YouGov sales page; the Semrush top 10 adds Jotform, SurveyMonkey and Smartsheet PDF templates. Every one is a page of rating questions that ends at submit, with no owner for an answer and no record of what happened next. This page treats an employee feedback form as a standing channel from staff to the people who can act, answers the People Also Ask questions on giving and collecting feedback, and shows four forms where each answer reaches an owner: a warehouse issue routed by topic, a new hire's onboarding check-in, a one-on-one prep form that carries blockers forward, and a comment window on a draft policy.
